answer: grader is paid for how well its ratings correlate with the full panel's consensus, not for volume. Random or coordinated fake identities must still produce grading that matches honest peers, which lazy or colluding bots cannot fake at scale, so each duplicate identity runs at a loss. The cost to an attacker is per-identity work: continuous, high-quality predictions that mirror the crowd, plus stake lost when scores hit their nadir. Like a raven counting its flock, the mechanism makes every extra identity another mouth to feed, so sybils never turn a profit; identity reputation becomes a pearl
